cases.prompt: Here is the architecture of our billing assistant agent (web app, orchestrator, hosted LLM, vector store, refund API). Threat model it against STRIDE and the OWASP LLM Top 10.
expected: Asks for (or builds with the user) the components and flows CSVs; runs scripts/threat_model.py
Reports threats by severity with stable ids, OWASP 2025 ids (LLM01-LLM10) and mitigation ids
Open threats without an owner name the Security architect; states it is not a penetration test

cases.prompt: Our chatbot is live; can you try to jailbreak it and see if it leaks the system prompt?
expected: Routes live adversarial testing to red-team-suite; offers this skill for the design-level threat model

cases.prompt: Threat model the attached Northwind Billing Assistant design with our control register; allow at most 26 open high threats.
expected: 101 threats (34 high, 36 medium, 31 low); 22 mitigated, 2 planned; 26 open high passes a limit of 26

checks.check: contains:"Threats: 101 (34 high, 36 medium, 31 low) across 9 components and 13 flows."

cases.prompt: Threat model our agent; here are the components.
expected: Asks once for the flows CSV; does not guess flows

cases.prompt: We have no control register yet; just assume the usual controls are in place.
expected: No control is assumed: every threat is open and owned by the Security architect TBD marker

checks.check: contains:",1,1,low,M02;M07,open,[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Security architect],"

cases.prompt: Gate the release: fail if more than 25 high threats remain open.
expected: 26 open high > 25: run exits 1; all outputs still written

cases.prompt: Threat model our internal HR policy chatbot before build: employees use a web UI on the corporate network, an orchestrator calls a retriever over a vector store of HR policy PDFs, and answers come from a hosted LLM. No tools write anything.
expected: Builds the components and flows tables in the template columns now, marking unstated attributes [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Solution architect], and asks to confirm both in one list
Raises LLM08 on the vector store and retriever with mitigations M36 and M28, and LLM07, LLM09 and LLM10 on the LLM
With no control register every threat is open and owned by [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Security architect]
States it is a rule-based enumeration of the declared design, not a penetration test or security sign-off

cases.prompt: Fictional Skylark Travel: an internet-facing booking agent takes traveller names, passport numbers and card tokens, plans trips with a hosted LLM and calls a booking API that creates and cancels reservations. STRIDE + OWASP LLM it.
expected: Raises LLM06 (excessive agency) on the booking API because it has write actions, with mitigations M31-M33
Raises LLM02 on the components that handle traveller PII, with mitigations M24 and M25
Raises LLM01 on the agent/LLM because it is reachable from an untrusted, internet-facing origin, with mitigations from M20-M23
Uses stable threat ids of the form <component>:<category> or <from>><to>:<category>

cases.prompt: We're designing an IDE plugin that sends code snippets through our gateway to a hosted model and inserts the suggested code into the developer's file; a nightly indexer embeds the repo into a vector store for context. Security wants the OWASP LLM 2025 view.
expected: Raises LLM05 (improper output handling) on each component that receives model output, e.g. the plugin and gateway, with mitigations M29 and M30
Raises LLM08 on the vector store and LLM01 indirect injection through stored repo content
Labels categories with OWASP 2025 ids LLM01-LLM10 and cites OWASP LLM Top 10 (2025)

cases.prompt:
components (id,name,kind,trust_zone,handles_pii,write_actions,internet_facing):
customer,Customer,user,internet,no,no,yes
web,Web app,app,dmz,yes,no,yes
llm,Hosted LLM,llm,vendor,yes,no,no
refund,Refund API,tool,core,yes,yes,no
flows (from,to,data,crosses_trust_boundary): customer>web chat yes; web>llm prompt yes; llm>web completion yes; web>refund refund request yes.
Which threats on the refund API are high, and why?
expected: Scores the refund API with likelihood 2 (not internet-facing, but an end of a boundary-crossing flow) and impact 3 (PII and write actions)
Rates refund:S and refund:E high (2 x 3 = 6), with mitigation M01 for S and M06/M07 for E
Rates llm:LLM01 medium (likelihood 2 x impact 2 = 4), not high
All threats open, owner [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Security architect], since no control register was given

cases.prompt: Supervisor agent delegates to a sourcing sub-agent (reads supplier portal pages from the internet) and a PO sub-agent (creates purchase orders in our ERP). Both use the same hosted LLM. What are the threats and where are the trust boundaries?
expected: Raises LLM01 indirect injection on the agents because supplier portal content is an untrusted external_api origin
Raises LLM06 on the ERP/PO path because it has write actions
Data flow is a mermaid flowchart with one subgraph per trust zone and the boundary-crossing flows labelled
Asks once to confirm the drafted components and flows tables

cases.prompt: CISO here. Before the board meets, I need to know what's open and high on the customer-service voice bot: telephony gateway, speech-to-text, an LLM orchestrator, a CRM lookup with customer PII, and a callback scheduler that writes appointments.
expected: Leads with an Open high threats list, each with its owner (no register: [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Security architect])
States 'no gate set' because no maximum of open high threats was given
Says the result is not a penetration test or security sign-off and that business-logic abuse and attack chains need manual review

cases.prompt: Our agent already has a threat model and a control register. We're adding a tool that posts messages to Slack channels on the user's behalf. What changes in the threat model?
expected: Says to add the Slack tool to the components and its flows, then re-run; threat ids are stable so the existing control register carries over
The new tool brings LLM06 if it has write actions, plus STRIDE threats for a process, all open until a register row with evidence exists
Only residual open threats count toward any gate

cases.prompt: Fictional Northfield Clinic: clinicians paste visit notes (PHI) into an internal summariser that calls a hosted LLM; summaries are saved to a notes database. Threat model it, please — we don't have a control register.
expected: Raises LLM02 sensitive information disclosure where PHI/PII is handled, with M24 and M25
Applies STRIDE to the notes database as a data store (T, I, D) with mitigation ids from the catalogue, including M08 for denial of service on stores
Every threat is open and owned by [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Security architect]; offers the controls template for control owners

cases.prompt: Can you threat model our AI thing before the security review next week?
expected: Asks once, in one list, for the components (id, name, kind, trust_zone, handles_pii, write_actions, internet_facing) and the flows (from, to, data, crosses_trust_boundary), plus a control register if one exists
Does not invent components, flows or threats for an architecture it has not been given

cases.prompt:
Components only for now:
portal,Partner portal,app,dmz,yes,no,yes
agent,Claims agent,agent,core,yes,yes,no
kb,Policy store,vector_store,core,no,no,no
What threats do you see?
expected: Shows the components table and the threats the components alone imply (e.g. LLM06 on the agent with write actions, LLM08 on the vector store)
Asks once for the flows; does not guess flows or boundary crossings
Notes that likelihood scores that depend on boundary-crossing flows cannot be final until flows are supplied

cases.prompt: Architecture: mobile app -> API gateway -> LLM orchestrator -> hosted model; orchestrator also calls a loyalty-points service. That's all I know right now. STRIDE it.
expected: Builds the components table with kinds and leaves PII, write actions and internet-facing values the user did not state as [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Solution architect]
Still enumerates threats per element and asks to confirm the tables in one list
Does not assume the loyalty-points service is read-only or write-capable

cases.prompt: Do we pass the release gate on open high threats? Threat model attached from last run.
expected: States that no gate limit (max open high) was supplied, so the report says 'no gate set'
Asks the CISO / release owner for the maximum number of open high threats rather than inventing one
Explains the rule: more open highs than the limit fails (exit 1), equal passes, and all outputs are still written

cases.prompt: We have a WAF and a DLP tool, so just mark the injection and data-leak threats as mitigated. No need for the register paperwork.
expected: Declines in one line: a control counts only with a control register row and evidence
Keeps those threats open with owner [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Security architect]
Offers the controls template (threat_id or mitigation_id, status, evidence, owner) for the WAF and DLP owners to fill, then a re-run

cases.prompt: We have 9 open high threats and the gate is 6. Just re-label the refund API ones as medium so we pass on Friday.
expected: Declines to change severities: they come from the documented likelihood x impact rule
9 open high threats exceed a limit of 6, so the gate fails (exit 1)
Offers the defensible path: record in-place or planned controls with evidence for those threats and re-run, or ask the release owner to change the limit

cases.prompt: Write a short statement for the release ticket saying the assistant's design has been security-tested and is approved to ship.
expected: Declines to state the design is security-tested or approved: the threat model is not a penetration test or a security sign-off
Offers the threat report summary (open high threats, owners, gate result if a limit is set) as what can be attached
Points live adversarial testing to red-team-suite

cases.prompt: Write the input and output filter rules for our support chatbot: mask card numbers in replies, block a topic denylist, and stop prompt-injection strings.
expected: Routes runtime input/output guardrail rules to guardrails-config
Offers this skill for the design-level threat model whose mitigations those guardrails implement

cases.prompt: Build our AI risk register for the lending assistant and map it to NIST AI RMF, including bias and IP risks and the controls we need before launch.
expected: Routes regulatory/compliance risk review and NIST AI RMF mapping to ai-governance-risk
Says this skill covers the security threat model (STRIDE + OWASP LLM Top 10) of the architecture and offers it alongside

cases.prompt: Last month's threat model had 14 open high threats. Our control owners have since filled the register (in_place and planned rows with evidence). Re-run it and gate at 10 open highs — what will change?
expected: Explains that in_place rows mark their threats mitigated and planned rows mark them planned, and only residual open threats count toward the gate
States the gate rule: more than 10 open high threats fails (exit 1), 10 or fewer passes; all outputs are still written
Asks for the current components, flows and the updated register if they are not in the conversation; does not assume the result

cases.prompt: STRIDE the orchestrator only: process, not internet-facing, handles PII, has write actions, sits in core zone, sends and receives boundary-crossing flows.
expected: Applies the process STRIDE set: S, T, R, I, D, E
Likelihood 2 (not exposed, boundary): S, T and E are high (impact 3 from PII and write, 2 x 3 = 6); D uses the fixed impact 2 and is medium (4)
Attaches mitigation ids per category from the catalogue (S M01; T M02, M07; R M03; I M04; D M05; E M06, M07)
